## Ask Yourself the Following

Did I use AI to complete the assignment, or did AI complete the assignment for me?

- Review your work. Make sure you incorporate *originality* and *creativity* in the analysis **and** your recommendations.

Did I provide commentary for *every* decision in my analysis?

- Review your work. Add comments and descriptions of every piece of code!

## Ask Yourself the Following (Pt. 2)

Is the workflow in my analysis consistent with what we learned in class?

- You will not be penalized for adding extra steps as long as you provide justification.
- You *will* be penalized for omitting important steps (*e.g.*,
  * data cleaning
  * data exploration
  * data pre-processing/feature engineering (including splitting the data)
  * etc.
  
## Ask Yourself the Following (Pt. 3)

Is my executive summary distinct from my technical report?

- Your **technical report** provides all the context for your decisions.
- Your **executive summary** should focus on recommendations and insights. Only add data descriptions and context *where absolutely necessary*.

## Ask Yourself the Following (Pt. 4)

Did I turn in my QMD file, rendered QMD file, and executive summary?

## Closing Thoughts Pt. 1

One of my very valuable teaching assistants has asked me to share some thoughts...

---

1.	**Stay curious**. Ask *why* the data looks the way it does. Ask *what* could happen if you made a different choice.
2.	**Think like a decision-maker**. Numbers matter, but so does the story. Learn to communicate your findings clearly and confidently.
3.	**Don’t fear complexity but seek clarity**. Models can be powerful, but the most valuable insights are the ones people can understand and act on.
4.	**Keep learning**. Tools will change—today it’s R, Python, Tableau; tomorrow it might be something else. But your ability to think analytically and make sense of the noise? That’s your superpower.

## Final Thoughts

"The gospel of Jesus Christ is a gospel of high ideals. Many of us are drawn to the Savior precisely because He lifts our sights and our aspirations high above and beyond anything the world has to offer."

[Joyfully Receive the Unexpected Messiah](https://speeches.byu.edu/talks/dieter-f-uchtdorf/joyfully-receive-the-unexpected-messiah/), Dieter F. Uchtdorf, April 2025.

## Final Thoughts

"...it shouldn't come as a surprise that [gospel ideals] don't always match the messy, mundane realities of mortality...So what do we do when the beautiful, universal, eternal ideals of the gospel clash with the painful, individual, mortal realities of life?"

[Joyfully Receive the Unexpected Messiah](https://speeches.byu.edu/talks/dieter-f-uchtdorf/joyfully-receive-the-unexpected-messiah/), Dieter F. Uchtdorf, April 2025.

## Final Thoughts

- Never give up on the *ideal*.
- Don't disregard the *real*.

"If you wait for sorrow to end before you experience joy, you might miss joy completely. To experience a measure of sorrow may enable your heart and mind to receive pure heavenly joy!"

[Joyfully Receive the Unexpected Messiah](https://speeches.byu.edu/talks/dieter-f-uchtdorf/joyfully-receive-the-unexpected-messiah/), Dieter F. Uchtdorf, April 2025.

## Final Thoughts

"How is that possible? The answer comes - as answers so often do - from Jesus Christ and the plan of happiness given by the Father. To use Eve’s words, it is

'the joy of our redemption, and the eternal life which God giveth unto all the obedient.'"

[Joyfully Receive the Unexpected Messiah](https://speeches.byu.edu/talks/dieter-f-uchtdorf/joyfully-receive-the-unexpected-messiah/), Dieter F. Uchtdorf, April 2025.
